- Rows 27-29: full-width bar at columns 12-23 (B2's top bar overlapping with B1's vertical bar).
- Rows 30-32: full-width bar at columns 12-23 (B1's bottom bar + B2's stem at columns 15-18).
So B2 is at (27,12,32,23): top bar rows 27-29, stem rows 30-32 columns 15-18. B1 is at (21,12,32,23).
B2's target is (42,9,47,20). From (27,12,32,23): 15 DOWN, 3 LEFT.

Note: B2's target (42,9,47,20) is Y3's position. Y3 is at (42,9,47,20) — B2 will end up sitting on top of it.
Batch cap is 10 per action() call. 15 DOWN + 3 LEFT = 18 → split into 2 calls: 10 DOWN, then 5 DOWN + 3 LEFT.
After that: SPACE (→B1), B1 from (21,12,32,23) → (42,33,53,44): 21 RIGHT + 21 DOWN = 42 actions → 5 calls of 10 + 1 call of 2.
After that: SPACE (→wall), 6 UP.
Total remaining: 18 + 1 + 42 + 1 + 6 = 68 actions.
Let's proceed with B2: 10 DOWN.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def get(fr):
    out={}
    for n in fr.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='B' and n['pixels']>20:
            b=n['boundary']; rows=[p[0] for p in b]; cols=[p[1] for p in b]
            out['black']=(min(rows),min(cols),max(rows),max(cols),n['pixels'])
    return out
action(['DOWN']*10)
print("after 10 DOWN:", get(current_frame))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
